transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I spend so much time checking and trying to fix this one thing about how I look that it’s taking over my day and costing me work. It has gotten to the point where I feel completely overwhelmed by it and just don't know what to do anymore.
Can you tell me more about what you're checking and trying to fix about your appearance, and how often you find yourself doing this?

I'm completely obsessed with how old and worn-out my face looks, especially the deep lines and the gray hair at my temples. Most days, I lose hours in front of the mirror taking selfies in different lights, changing shirts, and trying to hide it. I end up constantly texting my daughter or coworkers for reassurance until I'm so late and frustrated that I just cancel my plans altogether.
Can you estimate how many times a day you feel compelled to check your appearance or seek reassurance from others about how you look?

It happens so constantly throughout the day that it’s honestly hard to count. I easily lose several hours in front of the mirror taking selfies and changing clothes, and I’ll text my daughter or coworkers up to ten times a day asking if I look too old. It completely derails my schedule to the point where I can't get anything done.
Do you ever experience any intrusive thoughts or urges to perform specific rituals, such as excessive grooming or checking, in response to your concerns about your appearance?

Yes, I get these intense, uncontrollable urges that feel like rituals I absolutely have to complete. I'll spend hours in the bathroom mirror adjusting my hair to hide the gray, taking selfies in different lighting, and changing my shirt over and over again. It's like I'm trapped in this constant loop of grooming and checking just to try and feel okay enough to face people.
Do you feel like these urges to check and fix your appearance are driven by a fear of something bad happening, or are they more about trying to feel just right or perfect in your appearance?

It’s definitely more about a deep fear of being judged than trying to look perfect. I am absolutely terrified that people will look at me and think I look old, worn-out, and like I’ve completely let myself go. I constantly worry they are comparing me to my ex-wife's younger partner or my successful, polished clients.

Can you describe if your fear of being judged is specifically focused on the possibility of being rejected or ostracized by others due to your appearance, or is it more about the general discomfort of not meeting your own standards of attractiveness?

It is definitely about how others perceive and judge me, and the fear of being rejected. I constantly worry that people are comparing me to my ex's younger boyfriend or my polished clients and thinking I've let myself go. That fear of their silent judgment is what makes me want to withdraw and hide from everyone.

When you're able to momentarily stop checking or fixing your appearance, do you feel a sense of relief from the fear of judgment, or do you still feel a strong urge to continue perfecting your appearance even if no one is around to judge you?
I'm not quite sure, as I haven't really thought about it in those exact terms. The fear of how other people are judging me is just so constant that it's hard to separate the two.
Is your fear of being judged by others primarily driven by a concern that they will think you're unattractive, or is it more about being perceived as inadequate or incompetent in some way?

It is definitely about looking old and tired, which makes me worry that I look like I'm failing or don't measure up to my polished peers. Even though I know I am good at my job, looking worn-out makes me feel like I've let myself go and look inadequate compared to everyone else.

Can you clarify whether your excessive checking and fear of judgment are solely about your physical appearance, or if they also involve concerns about being judged as incompetent or failing in your role?

The checking and fear of judgment are entirely about my physical appearance, specifically looking old, gray, and worn-out compared to everyone else. While these worries have ended up hurting my work performance and causing me to dodge meetings, the root of my anxiety is strictly how I look, not a fear of being incompetent at my job.
Have you ever experienced excessive anxiety or fear that is not related to your appearance, such as fear of specific situations, objects, or activities?
No, I don't really have those kinds of fears or anxieties about other things or situations. My worry is almost entirely focused on how I look and how others perceive my appearance.

Can you tell me if your repetitive behaviors, such as checking and grooming, are primarily aimed at reducing your anxiety about your appearance, or if they are more about following a specific rule or ritual that you feel compelled to complete?

It isn't about following any rigid rules or rituals. My behaviors are completely driven by intense anxiety about looking old and worn-out, and my desperate attempts to hide my wrinkles and gray hair. I only check the mirror and ask for reassurance because I'm trying to ease that panic and hide how I look.
Have you ever experienced any obsessive thoughts or compulsions that are not related to your appearance, such as concerns about symmetry, contamination, or harm coming to yourself or others?

No, I don't experience anything like that. My obsessive thoughts and behaviors are strictly focused on my appearance and how old I look, rather than things like contamination, symmetry, or harm. It really is just about my face and hair.

You've mentioned that your obsessive thoughts and compulsions are strictly about your appearance, but can you think of any times when you've had obsessive thoughts or felt compelled to perform rituals that weren't related to how you look, even if they seem minor or insignificant?

No, I really can't think of any obsessive thoughts or rituals that aren't related to my appearance. Every single one of these worries and behaviors is strictly focused on how old and worn-out I look. There is nothing else in my life that triggers that kind of behavior.

Have you ever felt compelled to repeat certain actions or check things that have nothing to do with how you look, such as locking doors, counting, or arranging objects, even if it seems unrelated to your appearance concerns?
No, I don't experience those types of behaviors at all, like counting things or checking locks. My checking and repetitive habits are strictly focused on my appearance and how I look.

Are you certain that you've never experienced any obsessive thoughts or compulsions that aren't related to your appearance, such as a fear of germs, a need for symmetry, or repetitive thoughts that aren't about how you look?

Yes, I am absolutely certain. I have never experienced a fear of germs, a need for symmetry, or any other obsessive thoughts like that. My worries and repetitive habits are strictly focused on my appearance and looking old.

Can you confirm again that you have never had any recurring, intrusive thoughts or urges to perform specific rituals that are not related to your appearance, such as fears of harm, contamination, or needing things to be in a specific order?

Yes, I can absolutely confirm that. I do not experience any of those fears about harm, contamination, or needing things in a certain order, nor do I have any rituals related to them. My worries and repetitive behaviors are strictly and entirely focused on my appearance.

Is it possible that your obsessive thoughts and compulsions to check your appearance might be part of a broader pattern of obsessive-compulsive behaviors, or are they truly isolated to your concerns about looking old and worn-out?

They are completely isolated to my concerns about how I look. I don't experience any other typical obsessive-compulsive behaviors like handwashing, counting, or checking locks. My struggle is strictly about looking old, my gray hair, and the deep lines on my face.

Can you think of any situation or time when your excessive preoccupation with your appearance and the urge to check or fix it would temporarily stop or significantly decrease, such as when you're deeply engaged in an activity you enjoy or when you're alone?

I can't really think of any specific situations where the worry or checking completely stops or goes away. It feels pretty constant and hard to escape, even when I am by myself or trying to focus on other things.
Can you think of any situation where you would experience significant distress or anxiety that is not related to how you look or being judged based on your appearance?

I can't really think of any other major sources of anxiety right now. Almost all of my current distress, whether it's the trouble I'm having at work or the strain with my family, seems to ultimately tie back to my appearance concerns and my avoidance of being seen.

If you were to imagine yourself in a situation where your appearance was completely irrelevant, such as being alone in a dark room or wearing a full-face mask, would you still experience any obsessive thoughts or compulsions that are not related to how you look?

I really don't think I would experience those kinds of thoughts or behaviors if my appearance wasn't a factor. My worries and rituals are entirely focused on how I look, so without that concern, I don't think I would have any of those issues.
If you were able to completely eliminate your concerns about your appearance, do you think you would still experience any obsessive thoughts or compulsive behaviors in other areas of your life?

No, I really don't think I would experience those behaviors in other areas of my life. My worries and repetitive habits are entirely focused on my appearance, so I think they would disappear completely if that concern was gone.

You've consistently stated that your obsessive thoughts and compulsions are strictly about your appearance, but can you definitively say that you have never, even briefly, experienced any obsessive thoughts or felt compelled to perform any rituals that are completely unrelated to how you look?

Yes, I can definitively say that. I really cannot think of any other obsessive thoughts or rituals that are unrelated to my looks. My worries and habits have always been entirely focused on my appearance.

If you were to experience a significant improvement in your appearance concerns, such as waking up one day and feeling completely satisfied with how you look, do you think you would still have any obsessive thoughts or compulsions about other things in your life?
I'm not really sure, as I haven't thought about it much. My worries and habits have been entirely focused on my appearance, so I don't think I would have obsessive thoughts about other things.

If you were to suddenly and completely stop worrying about your appearance, do you think you would then start to worry excessively about something else, or would your obsessive thoughts and compulsive behaviors completely disappear?

It is very difficult for me to even imagine a life where I'm not worrying about my appearance, since it currently consumes so much of my day. I'm really not sure if I would start worrying about something else, as I haven't ever thought about that possibility.
If you were to completely overcome your concerns about your appearance, do you think you would still experience any obsessive thoughts or compulsive behaviors, or would they completely resolve?

I'm not entirely sure since I haven't really thought about it that way. Currently, all of my obsessive worrying and checking behaviors are completely focused on my appearance, so it is hard to say what would happen if that went away.

If you were to experience a significant reduction in your obsessive thoughts about your appearance, do you think any other obsessive thoughts or compulsions would emerge or become more prominent in your life?

I haven't really thought about it, but I don't think any other obsessions would appear. My focus has been so entirely consumed by my appearance concerns that it's hard to imagine worrying about anything else.
Can you think of any past experiences or situations where you had obsessive thoughts or compulsions that were not related to your appearance, even if they seemed minor or insignificant at the time?
I cannot recall ever having any obsessive thoughts or compulsive behaviors that were unrelated to my appearance. My worries have always been focused entirely on how I look.

If you were to completely overcome your concerns about your appearance, do you think you would still experience any obsessive thoughts or compulsive behaviors that are not related to how you look, or would those completely resolve as well?

I don't think I would have any other obsessive thoughts or behaviors because I've never experienced them for anything else. My focus has been so entirely on my looks that I believe they would completely resolve.

Can you imagine a scenario where your appearance concerns completely disappeared, and if so, do you think you would then experience obsessive thoughts or compulsions about other aspects of your life, such as work, relationships, or health?

It's honestly hard to even imagine a scenario where my appearance concerns are completely gone because they take up so much of my mind right now. I'm really not sure if I would develop other obsessive thoughts, as I've never thought about that possibility.

If you were to completely overcome your concerns about your appearance, do you think you would still have the urge to perform any repetitive behaviors or experience obsessive thoughts that are not related to how you look?

No, I don't think I would have any of those urges or thoughts. All of my anxiety, mirror-checking, and reassurance-seeking are entirely driven by my worries about looking old and worn-out. Without those appearance concerns, I wouldn't have these urges at all.
